CAUSE 2, independent: the 30-day date-ranged query, which is the shape the page actually sends, also fails from THIS container (SERVER_ERROR then client_error on the permitted retry) and times out at our TIMEOUT_S from the droplet (504 at 15.7s). So that query is genuinely slow or erroring upstream for everyone. Two stacked causes on one panel is why 11-14 and 11-15 produced opposite, convincing, and both wrong shape correlations. THE DECISION, and all four options are outside the autonomous mandate: (a) get a free NVD API key and have feedproxy send it, which lifts the documented unauthenticated rate limit from 5 to 50 requests per 30s and is the option NVD itself recommends, but it is a new credential and needs somewhere to live; (b) change the proxy UA to a plain browser string, a fetch-policy change of the kind the 11-04 flexradio note deliberately put to James rather than making; (c) narrow the date window so the query stops straddling our 15s ceiling, which changes what the panel displays; (d) accept the panel failing and render a quieter placeholder. Worth deciding alongside cisa-advisories-feed-5xx: both are feedproxy fetch-policy questions and answering them one at a time keeps producing nights like this. NARROWED 2026-11-16 AFTER THE POST-DEPLOY LOAD, and this is the current position: the NVD panel SUCCEEDED post-deploy with the dated query from the droplet, about 20 minutes after the three 503s. So this is NOT a hard block and NOT a permanent refusal. The measurements above stand, but the defensible reading is that NVD's behaviour toward the droplet is intermittent and origin-sensitive: bursts of fast upstream 503s to us while an unrelated client is served normally, plus a 30-day dated query slow enough to hit our 15s ceiling. That pattern, intermittent 503s under light load, is the classic signature of unauthenticated per-IP rate limiting, which makes option (a), the free NVD API key, the most likely fix rather than merely one of four. It is still a new credential and still James's call. DO NOT CLOSE THIS on a single clean night: it has now flapped across 11-14, 11-15 and 11-16, and both of the last two runs nearly drew a wrong conclusion from one favourable observation.

awaiting_james.status: OPEN and the one NEW decision for James. This is the generalization of three separate items that have each been chased as their own bug: nvd-intermittent-origin-throttling, epss-cold-cache-504, and tonight's brand-new Google News 429. awaiting_james.detail: backend/feedproxy.py makes exactly ONE attempt per request and surfaces any failure straight to the page as a dead panel. Three upstreams have now been caught failing a first call and succeeding on an immediate identical retry from the same origin. TONIGHT'S MEASUREMENTS. Google News PQC: page load 502 'upstream returned 429' at 644ms and a .feed-error on screen; the IDENTICAL url then returned 200 with 31,197 bytes at 492ms, and the panel was clean on the second page load. NVD dated CRITICAL query: page load 504 'upstream feed timed out' at 15,834ms against TIMEOUT_S=15; the IDENTICAL url returned 200 in 1,072ms with 64,613 bytes and totalResults 68, and the panel was clean on the second load. EPSS did the same thing on 2026-09-17. Note the proxy caches ONLY successes (cache.set sits on the 200 path after a full body read), so each failure is a real independent refusal and each success is a real fetch, and the two orderings are not a caching artifact. THE DECISION, three options. (1) Add a single bounded retry inside /api/feed on 429, 502, 503 and timeout, with a short backoff of roughly 500ms to 1s and a hard ceiling so one slow upstream cannot pile up workers. Smallest change, kills most of the visible flapping, and it is squarely a backend behavior change, so this run did NOT make it. (2) Leave the proxy alone and have the two pages retry once client side before painting .feed-error. Keeps the backend untouched but has to be done in both standalone HTML files. (3) Accept intermittent blank panels as normal and stop reporting them, in which case say so and these three items can all be closed as working-as-intended. NOT DONE AUTONOMOUSLY because it changes shared backend behavior for every feed on the site, it affects timeout and concurrency characteristics, and the brief says to prefer reporting over guessing on anything less than certain. A retry also slightly changes data semantics by masking real upstream outages, which Step 5 reserves for James.
